newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits record high, Richter hits record.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits record high, Richter hits record.

text.p: The Budapest bourse's BUX index surged to a new record high in heavy volume on Tuesday, benefiting from a strong dollar and from the positive impact of pharmaceuticals Richter's first quarter results.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,952.92 points, up 103.51.

"The dollar certainly contributed to the rise but Richter spread a very optimistic sentiment to the market," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "I guess most other rising stocks benefited from Richter's gains."
Richter surged to a record high of 13,800 forints, before retreating to close at 13,650, up 950.
"Its (Richter's) first quarter was extremely strong," said Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London.
"It performed amazingly on the Russian markets, its sales to CIS countries grew by 40 percent in dollar terms," he said, adding this was beyond expectations.
Traders saimd interest was heavy in the market and this interest materialised in huge volume in oil company MOL and chemicals TVK.
"Investors try to buy those stocks which are still ahead of releasing their results," Keresztesi said, referring to expectations of strong earnings by TVK.
TVK closed at 2,805 forints, up 65 with close the 500,000 shares changing hands.
Traders said the market expects strong earnings from MOL too, but the main driving force, at least by domestic investors, is their fear of being unable to get stocks in MOL's public offer in May.
In heavy volume of over 369,000 units MOL shares surged 130 forints to close 3,380.
Elsewhere on the market, pharmaceuticals Egis fell 150 forints to end at 11,600 and traders said some investors might have unloaded Egis from their portfolio to buy Richter instead.
Clothes retailer, which said it planned to raise 100 million forints via a public bond issue, rose 700 forints to 7,900.
